A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mobile-R1 and retain the same core framework and Chinese dataset. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, training-stage comparisons, physical-device evaluations, pass@k tests and unseen-application analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, a Stage 2 omission experiment and human validation of the GPT-4o judge.

M1.justification: The backbone, three-stage procedure, action space, GRPO objectives and reward components remain unchanged. Renaming Stage 2 and explaining screenshot-window versus textual-history inputs clarify the existing procedure; the Stage 2 omission is an ablation.

E1.justification: Table 4 extends English evaluation from AndroidControl to GUI-Odyssey, covering cross-app navigation, and AITZ. This substantially broadens benchmark coverage while retaining the Chinese training corpus, Chinese benchmark and physical-device scenarios.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the retained Chinese and AndroidControl comparisons are unchanged. OdysseyAgent becomes Odyssey-7B, with identical AndroidControl results. The added benchmarks extend the existing baseline roster rather than introduce new comparison methods.

E3.justification: v4 adds a control that skips Stage 2 and a blind judge-validation protocol: 30 trajectories stratified across five score levels, independently rated by three annotators using majority labels. Existing splits, training budgets and agent-performance metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds a qualitatively reported Stage 2 omission test addressing curriculum necessity. Appendix I adds human validation addressing trajectory-reward reliability. These introduce two substantive validation questions; the earlier pass@k, unseen-app, physical-device and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix I introduces human–judge agreement estimation, including Spearman correlation, Kendall correlation and quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa. This adds statistical assessment of judge reliability, without adding training-seed variability or confidence-interval reporting for the agent benchmarks.

E6.justification: v4 adds GUI-Odyssey results of 75.24 TM/53.11 EM and AITZ results of 77.05 TM/60.50 EM for Mobile-R1, alongside baseline results. It also reports reward stagnation when Stage 2 is skipped and 70% exact human–judge agreement. Table 3 and retained AndroidControl scores are unchanged. GUI-Odyssey rankings in Table 4 place OS-Atlas and Odyssey above Mobile-R1, contrary to prose naming Odyssey and Aguvis.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, reward definitions and trajectory formulation retain their mathematical content. Added discussion of sparse rewards, memory and group normalization is explanatory; no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The three-stage training, dataset and benchmark contributions remain. v4 adds the central claim that direct task-level training encounters sparse-reward convergence difficulties and presents the contribution more explicitly as a systematic training recipe, with no new RL algorithm claimed.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands explanations of Stage 2's bootstrapping role, the two-epoch stopping choice and tolerance to judge disagreement. It newly limits long-range visual recall to the screenshot window and explains the showcased self-correction through current-screen cues and retained textual history.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly documents the VRAM motivation for screenshot truncation and states that personal information was anonymized during collection and annotation. Training hyperparameters and resource-release statements remain unchanged. Despite new references promising its value in Appendix E, the numerical screenshot-window size W is still unspecified.

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion or citations for MobileSteward, InquireMobile, Mobilebench, AndroidLens and AITZ. It also refines novelty positioning toward a training recipe and reasoning-annotated Chinese data. The established related-work framework remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method framing, conclusion and limitations undergo substantial rewriting. Numbered subsections reorganize the narrative, limitations move before the references, and training analysis moves into a dedicated appendix. Author and affiliation text changes; Section 5.2 also introduces duplicated benchmark discussion.

P2.justification: The document is extensively re-typeset with changed typography and page geometry. Table 4 expands to span both columns; reward and pass@k plots move from the main text to appendices, and dataset-statistics tables move to the end. Existing graphical results are retained, with renumbering and a corrected tail-success caption.

improvement.justification: The added benchmark evidence, blind human check of the reward judge and clearer capability limits provide a modest overall gain. The gain is constrained by the qualitative-only Stage 2 omission report, duplicated evaluation prose and a new GUI-Odyssey ranking statement that conflicts with Table 4. The missing numerical window size also remains unresolved. These shortcomings limit the benefit of the additional validation.
